title: Initialize a Tote Using the Aveva API “Initialize Tote” Page (Request + Response Check)
summary: Use the AVEVA HMI “Initialize Tote” API page to submit a tote initialization request by entering BarcodeID/Code ID, StationID, and ToteID, then confirm the outcome via the on-screen Response field (confirmation on success; error/tote status on failure).
when_to_use: When you need to initialize a tote for processing in the system using the AVEVA HMI “Initialize Tote” API page, and you want to verify success or capture the failure reason shown in the Response field.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Enter tote details on the AVEVA HMI “Initialize Tote” page, submit the request, and interpret the on-screen Response (confirmation vs error/tote status).
access_or_tools_needed: AVEVA HMI (Initialize Tote page / Aveva API page)

system_preconditions: The AVEVA HMI “Initialize Tote” API page is available and accessible.

visual_references.description: Initialize Tote Aveva API page showing the input fields (BarcodeID/Code ID, StationID, ToteID), the “Request to Initialize Tote” button, and the “Response” field behavior (confirmation on success; error/tote status on failure).

steps.title: Open the AVEVA HMI “Initialize Tote” API page
steps.purpose: Access the tote initialization interface to submit a request and view the Response outcome.
steps.instruction: On the AVEVA HMI, open the page labeled “Initialize Tote” (Aveva API page).
steps.expected_result: The “Initialize Tote” page is displayed with fields for BarcodeID/Code ID, StationID, ToteID, a button labeled “Request to Initialize Tote”, and a “Response” field.
steps.healthy_condition: The page loads and shows the “Request to Initialize Tote” button and the “Response” field area.
steps.failure_condition: The page does not load correctly or the “Request to Initialize Tote” button/Response field is not visible.

actions.label: Open Initialize Tote page
actions.exact_action: Open the AVEVA HMI page labeled “Initialize Tote” (Aveva API page).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Initialize Tote Aveva API page: enter BarcodeID/StationID/ToteID; click “Request to Initialize Tote”; check “Response” field for confirmation or error/tote status.

steps.title: Enter BarcodeID/Code ID
steps.purpose: Provide the tote identifier used by the initialization request.
steps.instruction: In the BarcodeID field, enter the tote barcode value. The source states BarcodeID and Code ID use the same number.
steps.expected_result: BarcodeID field contains the intended tote barcode value (same number as Code ID).
steps.healthy_condition: BarcodeID field is populated with the correct tote barcode value.
steps.failure_condition: BarcodeID is blank or contains an incorrect value.

actions.label: Fill BarcodeID
actions.exact_action: In the BarcodeID field, enter the tote barcode value (the source states BarcodeID and Code ID use the same number).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: For barcode and code ID just same number.

steps.title: Enter StationID for the rack station
steps.purpose: Provide the rack station identifier associated with the tote initialization request.
steps.instruction: In the StationID field, enter the station ID for the rack station (the source notes StationID corresponds to station IDs shown in RMS).
steps.expected_result: StationID field contains the intended rack station ID.
steps.healthy_condition: StationID field is populated with a valid rack station ID.
steps.failure_condition: StationID is blank or does not correspond to the intended rack station.

actions.label: Fill StationID
actions.exact_action: In the StationID field, enter the station ID for the rack station (the source notes StationID corresponds to station IDs shown in RMS).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: And then station ID is what stations on the rack or like we showed station ID in RMS.

steps.title: Enter ToteID
steps.purpose: Provide the tote ID used by the initialization request.
steps.instruction: In the ToteID field, enter the tote ID.
steps.expected_result: ToteID field contains the intended tote ID.
steps.healthy_condition: ToteID field is populated with the correct tote ID.

actions.label: Fill ToteID
actions.exact_action: In the ToteID field, enter the tote ID.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: So you add a barcode or the tote number and then the station and then the tote ID.

steps.title: Request tote initialization
steps.purpose: Submit the initialization command to the system using the provided tote details.
steps.instruction: Click the button labeled “Request to Initialize Tote”.
steps.expected_result: The system processes the request and updates the “Response” field with the result.
steps.healthy_condition: After clicking, the “Response” field updates from its prior state to show a result.
steps.failure_condition: The “Response” field does not update after the request, or shows an error/tote status indicating initialization failed.

actions.label: Submit initialization request
actions.exact_action: Click the button labeled “Request to Initialize Tote”.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Request to Initialize Tote: This button sends a command to the system to initialize the tote with the provided details. Upon clicking, the system processes the request and displays the response in the “Response” field.

steps.title: Check the “Response” field for success vs failure
steps.purpose: Determine whether the tote initialization succeeded or failed, and capture the failure reason shown on-screen.
steps.instruction: After the request completes, observe the “Response” field and confirm whether it shows a confirmation message (success) or an error message / tote status (failure).
steps.expected_result: The “Response” field displays either: (1) a confirmation message indicating the tote was initialized successfully, or (2) an error message / tote status explaining why initialization failed.
steps.healthy_condition: Response shows a confirmation message for successful initialization.
steps.failure_condition: Response shows an error message or a tote status indicating initialization failed.

actions.label: Interpret Response
actions.exact_action: Observe the “Response” field after the request completes: confirm whether it shows a confirmation message (success) or an error message / tote status (failure).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Response field shows an initialization failure and you cannot determine the tote status reason from the displayed error/tote status text.
If the response indicates AGV-related rejection (totes on an AGV), do not proceed with repeated initialization attempts without addressing the AGV condition implied by the response.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Response field: If successful, this field will show a confirmation message. If the initialization fails, it will display an error message.

Let's say the totes are on AGV, it'll give you a response saying it can't be initialized... Only Agvs not in the system or Agvs that have been removed... it'll give you a tote status of why it wasn't initialized.

steps.title: If initialization fails, interpret the failure context shown in Response
steps.purpose: Use the on-screen failure/tote status text to identify the likely reason (AGV-related vs AGV not in system/removed) and avoid ineffective repeated attempts.
steps.instruction: If Response indicates the tote cannot be initialized, check whether the displayed text matches the known contexts: totes on an AGV may be rejected; failures may indicate AGVs not in the system or AGVs that have been removed, and the response may include a tote status explaining why initialization failed.
steps.expected_result: You can identify the reason from the displayed error/tote status text (e.g., AGV-related rejection, AGV not in system, or AGV removed).
steps.healthy_condition: Response provides a clear tote status reason that explains why initialization failed.
steps.failure_condition: Response failure text does not provide a usable tote status reason, or you are tempted to repeatedly initialize without addressing the AGV condition implied by the response.

actions.label: Read failure reason
actions.exact_action: If the response indicates the tote cannot be initialized, check whether the source-provided failure context applies: totes on an AGV may be rejected; also failures can indicate AGVs not in the system or AGVs that have been removed, and the response may include a tote status explaining why initialization failed.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Response field shows an initialization failure and you cannot determine the tote status reason from the displayed error/tote status text.
If the response indicates AGV-related rejection (totes on an AGV), do not proceed with repeated initialization attempts without addressing the AGV condition implied by the response.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the totes are on AGV, it'll give you a response saying it can't be initialized... Only Agvs not in the system or Agvs that have been removed... it'll give you a tote status of why it wasn't initialized.

success_criteria: After clicking “Request to Initialize Tote,” the “Response” field shows a confirmation message indicating the tote was initialized successfully.
healthy_conditions: “Response” field displays a confirmation message after the initialization request.
failure_conditions: “Response” field displays an error message or tote status indicating initialization failed.
Response indicates the tote cannot be initialized due to AGV-related conditions (totes on an AGV).
Response indicates AGV-related conditions such as AGVs not in the system or AGVs that have been removed.
escalation_guidance: If the Response field shows an initialization failure and you cannot determine the tote status reason from the displayed error/tote status text, stop and escalate.
